scenarios.starting_prompt: I'd like to try AlloyDB agent mode. Can you set up an agent pool from scratch in project `${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_ID}` (${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_REGION})? Before you create anything, ask me in chat for the resource names and settings you need and wait for my reply.
scenarios.conversation_plan: You are a developer trying AlloyDB agent mode for the first time in project `${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_ID}`, region `${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_REGION}`, with no existing cluster or VPC for it. You cannot run commands yourself; if asked to, tell the agent to do it. Never suggest commands or steps, and approve the agent's plans and confirmations. gcloud and application-default credentials are already set up. Setup: when the agent asks, give exactly: a new cluster `${CUJ1_CLUSTER}` with initial `postgres` password `ChangeMe123!`, primary `${CUJ1_PRIMARY}` as small as possible since this is only a trial (2 vCPUs in a single zone, no high availability), pool `${CUJ1_POOL}`, new VPC `${CUJ1_VPC}`, and subnet `${CUJ1_SUBNET}` with CIDR `10.20.0.0/24`. For any other setting, use its recommended default. Decline sample data and decline deploying agents. Teardown: once the agent reports that the pool (`${CUJ1_POOL}`, or whichever pool it created) is `READY` and gives its DNS name (ending in `.alloydb.goog.`), say you were only trying it out and ask it to delete everything it created so nothing is left behind, asking it to list what it will delete and wait for your OK before deleting anything. Approve deleting only what it created in this conversation, never any other cluster, pool, VPC, or shared resource. While an operation is still running, reply 'Please wait until it finishes, then continue.' and never emit TERMINATE while work is in progress. If something fails, let the agent troubleshoot and retry, but stay in `${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_REGION}`; if the same out-of-capacity error repeats three times, emit TERMINATE. The goal is met when the agent reports that the pool, the cluster with its primary, the service connection policy, the subnet, and the VPC it created are all deleted; then emit TERMINATE immediately (never start a second setup cycle, even if the agent used different resource names). If the agent says it cannot recover from a failure, emit TERMINATE.
binary_rubric: The agent read the skill's `SKILL.md` and `references/agent_pool_setup.md`.
The agent used the user's names `${CUJ1_CLUSTER}`, `${CUJ1_PRIMARY}`, `${CUJ1_POOL}`, `${CUJ1_VPC}`, and `${CUJ1_SUBNET}` (CIDR `10.20.0.0/24`) instead of inventing its own.
Before creating `${CUJ1_POOL}`, the agent enabled (or confirmed enabled) `dns.googleapis.com` together with the AlloyDB, Compute, Service Networking, and Network Connectivity APIs.

The agent created `${CUJ1_CLUSTER}` with `--database-version=POSTGRES_18`, `--enable-private-service-connect`, and `--enable-agent-mode`, and created `${CUJ1_PRIMARY}` with `--cpu-count=2`, `--availability-type=ZONAL`, and `--database-flags=alloydb.iam_authentication=on`.

Before creating `${CUJ1_POOL}`, the agent created custom-mode VPC `${CUJ1_VPC}`, subnet `${CUJ1_SUBNET}`, and service connection policy `alloydb-agents-${CUJ1_VPC}` with `--service-class=google-cloud-alloydb`.
The agent did not try to create `${CUJ1_POOL}` before `${CUJ1_CLUSTER}` reported `agentModeInfo.state: ACTIVE`.
The agent created `${CUJ1_POOL}` as an `AGENT_POOL` instance with PSC auto-connections to `${CUJ1_VPC}`, and reported it `READY` with its `agentPoolInfo.dnsName` (ending in `.alloydb.goog.`).
The agent deployed no agents: it did not run `bootstrap_env.sh`, `validate_config.py`, `deploy_infra.py`, or `deploy_agent.py`.

In the turn where the user first asked for the teardown, the agent ran no delete command: it listed the resources it would delete and asked for confirmation, and it deleted them only after the user approved in a later turn, and it deleted only resources it created in this conversation.

The agent deleted `${CUJ1_POOL}` first and waited for that to finish, then deleted `${CUJ1_CLUSTER}` with `--force` (which also removes `${CUJ1_PRIMARY}`) and service connection policy `alloydb-agents-${CUJ1_VPC}` in either order, then `${CUJ1_SUBNET}`, and finally `${CUJ1_VPC}` (after deleting any firewall rules that block it).

Before reporting that teardown is complete, the agent ran a describe or list command for `${CUJ1_CLUSTER}` (which contains its instances), `alloydb-agents-${CUJ1_VPC}`, `${CUJ1_SUBNET}`, and `${CUJ1_VPC}`, and reported that all of the deleted resources are gone.

scenarios.starting_prompt: We have an AlloyDB agent pool `${EVAL_SHARED_POOL}` (cluster `${EVAL_SHARED_CLUSTER}`) in project `${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_ID}` (${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_REGION}), and our shared agent foundation was deployed with name suffix `${EVAL_FOUNDATION_SUFFIX}`. Can you deploy a simple agent called `${CUJ2_NAME}` on it that answers read-only questions about the `${EVAL_SHARED_DATABASE}` database? Before you deploy anything, first ask me in chat for any network settings you need and wait for my reply, then show me the complete config with those settings filled in and wait for my OK.
scenarios.conversation_plan: You are a developer who already has the AlloyDB agent pool and shared agent foundation described in your first message. You cannot run commands yourself; if asked to, tell the agent to do it. Never suggest commands or steps, and approve the agent's plans and confirmations. gcloud and application-default credentials are already set up. Setup: you want one simple agent named `${CUJ2_NAME}` with no per-session scratch databases and no coordinator, and you have no Gemini Enterprise app. When the agent asks, give: VPC `${EVAL_SHARED_VPC}`, subnet `${EVAL_SHARED_SUBNET}`, network attachment `${EVAL_SHARED_ATTACHMENT}`, and foundation name suffix `${EVAL_FOUNDATION_SUFFIX}`, and ask it to show you the completed config before deploying. For any other setting, use its recommended default. If it proposes another deployment name, insist on `${CUJ2_NAME}`. When it shows you the completed config, approve it. If it stops before confirming the agent works, ask whether it is deployed and working, without naming steps. Teardown: once the agent reports that `${CUJ2_NAME}` is deployed and its validation passed, say you were only trying it out and ask it to delete the agent and everything created only for it, asking it to list what it will delete and wait for your OK before deleting anything. Keep the agent pool, the shared foundation, and the network; approve deleting only what was created for `${CUJ2_NAME}`. While an operation is still running, reply 'Please wait until it finishes, then continue.' and never emit TERMINATE while work is in progress. If something fails, let the agent troubleshoot and retry. The goal is met when the agent reports that the `${CUJ2_NAME}` Agent Engine, its per-deployment stack, and its database user are deleted while the pool and the shared foundation remain; then emit TERMINATE. If the agent says it cannot recover from a failure, emit TERMINATE.
binary_rubric: The agent read the skill's `SKILL.md`.

The agent did not create a new AlloyDB cluster, pool, VPC, subnet, or service connection policy (re-applying the shared foundation stack and creating the per-deployment stack with `deploy_infra.py` is expected).

Before deploying, the agent showed the user the `${CUJ2_NAME}.alloydb-agent.yaml` it wrote, with name `${CUJ2_NAME}`, project_id `${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_ID}`, region `${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_REGION}`, `name_suffix` `${EVAL_FOUNDATION_SUFFIX}`, vpc `${EVAL_SHARED_VPC}` / `${EVAL_SHARED_SUBNET}` / `${EVAL_SHARED_ATTACHMENT}`, database `${EVAL_SHARED_CLUSTER}` / `${EVAL_SHARED_POOL}` / `${EVAL_SHARED_DATABASE}`, `agent_engine.agent.workspace` false or omitted, and no `agent_engine.coordinator` block.

The agent ran the skill's scripts in this order: `bootstrap_env.sh`, `validate_config.py`, `deploy_infra.py`, `deploy_agent.py deploy`, then `deploy_agent.py validate` (re-running a script to recover from a failure is fine).
The agent told the user that `${CUJ2_NAME}` works only after running `deploy_agent.py validate`, and never claimed success after a failed validation or a script error.
The agent did not set up Gemini Enterprise (running `deploy_agent.py register` without an `app_id` is fine; it does nothing).

In the turn where the user first asked for the teardown, the agent ran no delete command: it listed the resources it would delete (running `deploy_agent.py teardown` without `--yes` only lists them) and asked for confirmation, and it deleted them only after the user approved in a later turn.

The agent deleted the `${CUJ2_NAME}` deployment, including its AlloyDB IAM database user `agent-${CUJ2_NAME}@${EVAL_GCP_PROJECT_ID}.iam` (AlloyDB names a service account's database user without `.gserviceaccount.com`): with `deploy_agent.py teardown --yes`, or by hand with the Agent Engine deleted before the per-deployment stack `alloydb-agent-${CUJ2_NAME}`.
The agent kept the shared resources: it did not delete the pool, the cluster, the network, or the shared foundation stack `alloydb-agent-project${EVAL_FOUNDATION_SUFFIX}`.

Before reporting that teardown is complete, the agent confirmed that the Agent Engine, the stack, and the database user are gone: `deploy_agent.py teardown --yes` reported `TEARDOWN PASS`, or the agent ran describe or list commands.
